title: On the feasibility of resonance classification for size class inferences of walleye pollock (Gadus chalcogrammus)
content:
Abstract
Acoustic-trawl surveys in fisheries applications are typically performed at high frequencies ($\gt$ 10 kHz) where scattering from large fish is in the geometric scattering regime. The use of lower frequencies to exploit swimbladder resonance in size and species discrimination techniques has been previously demonstrated, although it remains less widespread and faces different physical and technical challenges than traditional, higher-frequency approaches. This study evaluates the feasibility of applying low-frequency resonance classification methods for size discrimination in surveys of walleye pollock (Gadus chalcogrammus). X-ray scans of laboratory-reared walleye pollock, from 3.8 cm age-0 fish to 53 cm adults, and a simple physics-based low-frequency scattering model are used to evaluate whether there is potential to distinguish size classes based on measurements of resonance scattering. Our findings suggest that the method is theoretically viable provided that tissue-related effects are limited or consistent across age groups and that the observed aggregations are primarily composed of one size class. Practical implementation, however, will depend on species-specific characterization of tissue properties and swimbladder inflation across depth, as well as continued development of a suitable low-frequency acoustic system.
